# E4 — the fast refresh: can the profile be refreshed without running the program again, and can the model's own report of the dependences close what that leaves open?

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** running

## The question

After the model has rewritten a loop, the agent profiles the whole program again; the fast refresh compiles only and carries the last run's dependences over, so the code the model just wrote has no measurement. Does that change whether the agent keeps a rewrite (H6's second half), does the model's own report of the dependences of its new lines repair it (H7), is adding dependences safe where deleting them is not (H7b) — and how many seconds does one refresh save where the run is long? In four steps, the cheap ones first (the author, 12 Oct): (1) the saved rewrites of the model replayed without a model, (2) the model's report on the rewrites that differ, (3) the time on programs with a long run, (4) live trials only if steps 1 and 2 say the refresh keeps DiscoPoP's verdicts. (RQ6, RQ7, C3)

## Result in one paragraph

Step 1 is read out (12 Oct; `e4_replay`, no model, 33 minutes on the server): 599 of the 601 pragma-free rewrites that passed the checks in the trials of E1-v6, E3 and E3b were judged after a fast refresh, after a full re-profile and after a second full re-profile as the control. The fast refresh changes whether the agent keeps the rewrite in 58 of 599, the control in 0 — the registered test E4-1: p = 0.000326, at most 0.0176 in the campaign's family of 54: H6's second half is refuted. 22 rewrites are kept only after the full re-profile — 20 of them loops the model turned into a reduction, for which the fast refresh makes DiscoPoP write `firstprivate` of the accumulator, a directive the agent's clause check refuses — and 13 of the 22 are rewrites their trial shipped; 2 are kept only after the fast refresh; 34 are kept after both with other directives, 27 of those differing only in a redundant `shared` clause (counted as the same, not registered: 31 differ, p = 0.000977, bound 0.0527). DiscoPoP's verdict on the rewritten lines differs in 417 of 599 (control 0). No time is saved on these loops: one refresh 1.54 s against 1.75 s, and with the gate's checks on the extra directives 1,758 s against 1,730 s in total. Step 3 is read out (12 Oct; `e4_refresh_time`, no model): where the profiling run is long one fast refresh saves 36 s on `hotspot` (33 % of a full re-profile; the explorer's own time there moves between 52 and 129 s), 27 s on `is` (66 %), 21.5 s on `md` (63 %) and 4.2 s on `correlation` (54 %) — 1.5 to 7.5 % of an agent trial on those programs — and on an unchanged program its Do-All and reduction loops are those of a full profile. Step 2 is prepared without a model: a hand-written correct report gives DiscoPoP the reduction back on three of the lost rewrites (a minimum, a sum, a maximum), and the dry pass `e4_report_dry` shows a run over all 599 rewrites sends 599 report requests while the deletion review has something to ask on 21 rewrites only, none among the 58 that differ; the fast refresh repeats itself on 599 of 599. Step 2's model calls wait for the author's choice (137 calls for the 58 that differ, 58 that do not and the 21; 620 for all); step 4 is not decided.

Against P: the same; kept only after the full re-profile (a win lost); kept only with X (a keep the full profile does not make — the 'unsafe' side of the hypotheses' wording); kept after both with other directives. No model has been called; none is called before the author has the exact cost.** **Why a pilot first** (the standing rule): step 2 asks whether the model's own account of the dependences of its rewrite gives DiscoPoP back what the fast refresh loses. Before that is paid for, it has to be seen that a CORRECT account does. **The pilot** (the Mac, 12 Oct, TSVC loops only; `results/E04_fast_refresh/analysis/report_pilot/`): for three of the 20 reductions of step 1 — a minimum (`s316`, repeat 1 of `e3b_1`, rewrite 1: `x = fmin(x, a[i]);`), a sum (`s319`, repeat 1 of `e3b_2`, rewrite 2: `sum += a[i] + b[i];`) and a maximum (`s3113`, repeat 2 of `e3b_2`, rewrite 1: `max = fmax(max, val);`) — the profile before the rewrite and the fast refresh are rebuilt with the replay tool, a report written by hand in the format the model is asked for (one line: `LOOP 9 RAW x 10 10`) goes through the agent's own `dep_reconstruct.reconstruct`, the explorer runs again and the rewrite is judged again as in step 1. **In all three** the line is placed as one row of the dependence file, DiscoPoP then writes the reduction on the model's loop — `reduction(min:x)`, `reduction(+:sum)`, `reduction(max:max)`, the directives of the full re-profile — the gate passes it, and the rewrite is kept. With the write-write dependence added as well the result is the same; a report that calls the loops independent changes nothing (the rewrite stays lost). After the fast refresh the reduction file already holds the entry for the model's loop in all three (the compile writes it): only the dependence was missing. On `s316` and `s3113` DiscoPoP still offers a directive on the repetition loop as well, which the race detector refuses as before; on `s319` the verdict is exactly the full profile's. **What this shows and what it does not:** the path from a correct report to the kept reduction works on the three operators; whether the model writes that report, and what its reports do to the rewrites whose decision the fast refresh did not change, is step 2's question. **The opposite direction on the three** (the model deletes dependences it calls unreal): the agent's review asks only about Do-All blockers that come from static analysis and lie in the rewritten lines; on the three there is none (no blocker recorded in two, one of measured origin in the third), so nothing would be asked. The fast refresh leaves these loops unblocked, not over-blocked. Where the review has anything to ask is counted by the dry pass. **Its texts have not been shown to the author** (`_SYSTEM_DEPS` and the request of `dep_review.review_dependences`), and two of its sentences are not exactly what the agent does: 'You are given the variable, the loop it blocks, and the two source lines' (the request names the two lines only where DiscoPoP recorded them; otherwise it shows the loop) and 'a dependence wrongly called spurious produces a racy parallel loop' (the loop can then look parallel to DiscoPoP; a directive on it still has to pass the checks). No deletion request is sent before he has seen them. **The tool:** `tools/report_replay.py`, on top of step 1's (`refresh_replay.Bench`). Per rewrite: the profile before, the fast refresh with verdict and judgement (as step 1); then from that refreshed profile (a) the request the agent sends after a rewrite has passed the checks (`ask_after_gate`, the approved text; the excerpt and loop list built as phase A builds them), the reply through `reconstruct`, the explorer again where a row was placed, verdict and judgement; (b) from the refreshed profile again — the agent never combines the two — the agent's `_llm_dep_review`, verdict and judgement; then the full re-profile. The agent's code is not changed. A rewrite whose model call failed is not written to the results and is asked again; three failures in a row stop the run.
